candidates.name: Nora Bennett
candidates.profile: An integration-minded project organiser. Favours clear interfaces and explicit reporting boundaries.
candidates.view: A delegation needs a named owner, a funded scope and a reason to return to your desk.

candidates.name: Adrian Cole
candidates.profile: An experienced mobilisation manager. Emphasises throughput and decisions before every uncertainty is resolved.
candidates.view: Keep investigations moving, but distinguish a working assumption from a demonstrated capability.

candidates.name: James Mercer
candidates.profile: A propulsion specialist with a strong test discipline. Direct in disagreement; less comfortable coordinating unrelated work.
candidates.view: A promising calculation is a reason to build a rig, not a reason to declare the engine understood.

candidates.name: Helen Ward
candidates.profile: A development engineer with practical manufacturing experience. Favours serviceable designs and early demonstrations.
candidates.view: Manufacturing access and repeatable tests are part of the design, not matters for later.

candidates.name: Rebecca Hayes
candidates.profile: A systems engineer attentive to instrumentation, cabin hazards and interactions between components.
candidates.view: If our instruments only see the isolated part, our confidence should stop at the interface.

candidates.name: Dr Maya Chen
candidates.profile: A physiologist concerned with exposure limits and the distance between laboratory evidence and a crewed flight.
candidates.view: A procedure must protect a person under the conditions they will actually experience.

candidates.name: Thomas Reed
candidates.profile: An operations organiser experienced in tracking networks, communications and rehearsal coordination.
candidates.view: The network, the procedures and the people have to work together before a flight makes them urgent.

candidates.name: Dr Lila Ortiz
candidates.profile: An independent reviewer who separates evidence from advocacy. Will challenge an attractive schedule when its claims exceed the records.
candidates.view: Tell me what the observation establishes, what it leaves open and who is accountable for the next claim.

propulsion.name: Scalable launch vehicles
propulsion.question: Which propulsion and integration assumptions can support larger launch vehicles?
propulsion.caveat: Ground development evidence does not qualify a particular launch vehicle or flight.

spacecraft.name: Spacecraft and safe return
spacecraft.question: What evidence is needed for a survivable cabin and controlled return?
spacecraft.caveat: Laboratory and prototype observations do not establish operational crew safety.

human.name: Human spaceflight research
human.question: How should exposure limits, procedures and crew protection be investigated?
human.caveat: The programme models research capability, not individual human-subject experiments or medical outcomes.

operations.name: Tracking and flight operations
operations.question: Can the tracking network, communications and teams support a coherent mission?
operations.caveat: Rehearsal evidence is scoped to its conditions; it is not an operational flight result.

events.title: An expanding institutional remit
events.detail: Historical context: JPL transferred to NASA in December 1958. In this prototype, institutional transfers remain aggregate background; they do not grant free research results or named appointments.

events.title: Longer-term objectives are entering discussion
events.detail: Planning beyond the first human flights increases the importance of propulsion, spacecraft, operations and credible evidence. Your research record determines what this agency can actually claim.

events.title: Gagarin reaches orbit
events.detail: External historical development: the Soviet Union reports Yuri Gagarin's orbital flight. This changes the political context, not the capability or results of your research teams.
